chunks.section_header: qSOFA Bedside Triage and Sepsis Red Flags
chunks.text_content: In non-ICU and outpatient settings, the quick Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (qSOFA) identifies adult patients with suspected infection at elevated risk of in-hospital mortality. A score of >=2 out of 3 criteria warrants immediate emergency escalation: (1) Altered mental status (Glasgow Coma Scale <15 or new confusion/somnolence), (2) Systolic blood pressure <=100 mmHg, and (3) Respiratory rate >=22 breaths per minute. Additional red flags include non-blanching purpuric skin rash, persistent anuria (>12 hours without urination), mottling of extremities, and profound rigors with hypothermia (<36.0 C / 96.8 F) or hyperpyrexia (>38.5 C / 101.3 F).

The SSC 1-Hour Bundle stipulates immediate initiation upon recognition of sepsis or septic shock: (1) Measure blood lactate level (remeasure if initial lactate >2 mmol/L), (2) Obtain blood cultures prior to administering broad-spectrum antimicrobials, (3) Administer empirical broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, (4) Rapidly administer 30 mL/kg crystalloid fluid for hypotension or lactate >=4 mmol/L, and (5) Initiate vasopressors (norepinephrine first-line) if patient remains hypotensive during or after fluid resuscitation to maintain mean arterial pressure (MAP) >=65 mmHg.
